title_en: The refusal to enter the holy land
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. This is an EVENT draft: it is shorter than the prophet drafts, stays inside the event's own inventory refs and states only what those ayat state; the prophet stories (content/stories) are not repeated here. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: Musa said to his people: remember God's favour to you, when He placed prophets among you, made you kings, and gave you what He had given to no one else in the worlds.
He told them to enter the holy land that God had written for them and not to turn back, or they would turn about as losers.
They said that powerful people were in it, and that they would not enter until those people left; if they left, they would enter.
A pair of men from those who feared, whom God had favoured, said: enter upon them by the gate, and when you have entered you will be the victors; and put your trust in God, if you are believers.
They said they would never enter as long as those people were in it, and told Musa to go, he and his Lord, and fight, for they would sit where they were.
Musa said: my Lord, I control only myself and my brother, so separate us from the disobedient people.
God said that it is forbidden to them for a stated number of years, in which they would wander in the land, and told Musa not to grieve over the disobedient people.

chapters.summary_md: Musa told his people to enter the holy land that God had written for them, and they refused to enter while powerful people were in it [c2][c3][c5]. God said it is forbidden to them for a stated number of years, in which they would wander in the land [c7].
chapters.body_md:
Musa reminded his people of God's favour: He had placed prophets among them, made them kings and given them what He had given to no one else in the worlds [c1]. He told them to enter the holy land that God had written for them and not to turn back, or they would turn about as losers [c2].

They said that powerful people were in it, and that they would not enter until those people left [c3]. A pair of men from those who feared, whom God had favoured, told them to enter upon them by the gate and to put their trust in God, if they were believers [c4].

The people said they would never enter as long as those people were in it, and told Musa to go, he and his Lord, and fight, for they would sit where they were [c5]. Musa said that he controlled only himself and his brother, and asked God to separate them from the disobedient people [c6].

God said that it is forbidden to them for a stated number of years, in which they would wander in the land, and told Musa not to grieve over the disobedient people [c7].
chapters.deep_md: The pair of men speak as believers who trust in God, and the ayah says that God had favoured them [c4]. The people answer first by setting a condition on entering and then by refusing outright [c3][c5]. The Arabic phrase for a stated number of years can be read with the prohibition or with the wandering [c7].
chapters.kids_md: Musa told his people to go into the holy land that God had written for them [c2]. They were afraid of the powerful people there and said they would not go in [c3][c5]. Musa asked God to separate him and his brother from them, and God said they would wander in the land for a stated number of years [c6][c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat contrast fear of powerful people with trust in God, as the pair of men put it [c3][c4]. Another is that Musa is told not to grieve over a people who stayed disobedient [c7].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which land the holy land is, where Musa and his people stood, or how long after leaving their former home this happened.
- Not established: who the powerful people were, or the names of the pair of men; the ayah says only that they feared and that God had favoured them.
- Not established: whether the years attach to the prohibition or to the wandering, or whether the prohibition ended; the Arabic allows both readings.
- Not established: what became of Musa and his brother in that time.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on this refusal and on the years of wandering. None is used in this draft.
The grammar of 'forbidden to them, years' (5:26) is read in more than one way by commentators; a scholar should choose the wording.
The identification of the holy land with a particular place comes from later tradition, not from the ayat.

The ayah states the number of years; this draft does not write it out because the shared number-word check has no anchor for it (its test keeps that word refused). A scholar should decide how the page states it.
